column1: # The cycle sweep's findings, RE-MEASURED with one row at a time per host (2026-10-20).
# tools/audit_cycle_health.py --ids-file <the 22 non-healthy verdicts + the 35 rows added since> --jobs 6
# WHY. The first full sweep (2026-10-19, 530 rows, 12 jobs — docs/cycle-health-2026-10-19.tsv) reported 12
# STUCK, 6 FETCH_FAILED and 4 SLOW, and the write-up hedged: "several are load this sweep created". A hedge is
# not a measurement. core/hostgate.c paces requests inside ONE process and cannot pace twelve that each think
# they are alone, and a cycling row makes ~20 requests to one host, so two rows of the same host overlap for
# their whole run. audit_cycle_health.py now serialises per host; this is the same rows asked again.
# SCOPE, and why it is not all 565: load makes a page FAIL, so it can only manufacture a false STUCK or
# FETCH_FAILED. It cannot manufacture a false CYCLING or COMPLETE, because those mean a position was or was not
# stored after a walk that WAS served. So the first sweep's 508 healthy verdicts stand, and only its 22
# findings needed re-reading — plus the 35 rows main added after that sweep ran (530 -> 565).
# RESULT: 43 CYCLING, 7 STUCK, 4 FETCH_FAILED, 2 COMPLETE, 1 SLOW. SEVENTEEN of the 22 verdicts CHANGED.
# Six of the twelve STUCK rows were the sweep's own load, now reading CYCLING:
#   FAA_ARCGIS_OBSTACLES         p20/429 -> CYCLING      FAA_ARCGIS_US_AIRPORTS   p18/429 -> CYCLING
#   us-sf-311-open311-requests   p20/429 -> CYCLING      au-asic-afs-licensees     p3/403 -> CYCLING
#   au-asic-credit-licensees      p4/403 -> CYCLING      (and UKPARL/GBIF rows from SLOW/FETCH_FAILED)
# One was real and is FIXED: BC_MINERAL_TENURE p2/400 -> CYCLING, after sortBy=TENURE_NUMBER_ID.
# THE au-asic FAMILY IS NOT FULLY EXPLAINED, and this is the honest remainder. Five rows share data.gov.au.
# Host-paced, two now cycle, two read FETCH_FAILED (403 on page 1) and one is still STUCK (403 on page 2). So
# the 403s are NOT purely this sweep's concurrency — which is what the earlier by-hand test suggested when
# data.gov.au served 8 rapid serial and then 12 concurrent requests, all 200, from urllib. The difference
# between that test and these runs is the CLIENT: the engine sends its own headers. That is the next thing to
# measure on this host, and it is recorded here rather than guessed at with a hostgate entry.
# The other four STUCK are 429 (ENERGINET, TRONSCAN, us-courtlistener), 500 (TZ_PPRA) and two transport
# failures (-1: CR_HEREDIA_PATENTES, WHO_XMART_FLUNET_SENTINEL, both previously SLOW and so unmeasured).
# Each still discloses its own failing page, status and URL on every run, so re-running this is how a
# transient stays distinguishable from a property.
